scope: Bounded read-only review of the exact installed Playwright dependency: public URL-based chromium.connectOverCDP attachment, browser.close and context.close ownership.

findings.fact: Public package entry exports the in-process Playwright client from lib/coreBundle.js.

URL connectOverCDP creates a WebSocket transport and synthetic browserProcess.close/kill handler that disconnects transport and removes Playwright-owned temporary artifact directories. Public browser.close reaches this handler through the channel and dispatcher; it does not itself issue native Browser.close, send an OS termination signal or reap the externally launched Chromium process.

CDP default context has no explicit browserContextId and is classified persistent. Its context.close routes to browser.close, disconnecting the entire attachment; it does not independently dispose the external default browser context.

browser.newContext creates a distinct CDP browserContextId with disposeOnDetach:true. Closing that context sends Target.disposeBrowserContext for its id. This is a real browser context/page disposal request, separate from termination of the browser process.
Transport disconnect tears down Playwright sessions, page/context model objects and emits Browser.Disconnected. These are not observations of external Chromium PID exit.
The bundled Chromium launch shutdown hook sends native Browser.close, but URL-based CDP attachment installs its own transport-disconnect handler instead of that launch path.

Default context close may dismiss tracked beforeunload dialogs before disconnect. Targets with browserContextIds not in the attachment-created context map fall back to the default context model; appearance through that model is not evidence of caller ownership.

practicalScope.browserClose: Close the Playwright CDP attachment and Playwright-owned temporary artifacts.
practicalScope.explicitContextClose: Request disposal of the created browser context/pages before attachment close.
practicalScope.externalLauncher: Separate caller-owned process cleanup and bounded observation remain required for the externally launched Chromium process.
unknowns: This source-only review does not observe Chromium context disposal response, browser PID exit, launcher process handling or descendant processes.
disposeOnDetach is a Chromium CDP request; no runtime detach or disposal was performed.
The conclusion covers the public URL endpoint path without a custom transport or internal onClose callback.
No atomic no-descendants claim follows from this dependency code.
